routes: rewrite | bound | deny_steer | output_gate | observe | exempt; pre=- means the input side has nothing to do

antigravity  (rewrite input: read_file, run_command only, replace output: no)
  pre=rewrite     post=observe      run_command
  pre=bound       post=observe      read_file
  pre=deny_steer  post=observe      view_file, grep_search, find_by_name, list_dir, ListDir, glob_search, codebase_search
  pre=observe     post=UNHOOKED     write_to_file, replace_file_content, multi_replace_file_content, edit_file
  pre=-           post=UNHOOKED     <unlisted tool>
  pre=-           post=observe      search_web, read_url_content, invoke_subagent, manage_task, mcp__<server>__<tool>
  exempt                           schedule, list_permissions, ask_permission, define_subagent, send_message, manage_subagents, ask_question
      why: session control or bookkeeping; returns a short status, and some results are the user's own answer or approval
  exempt                           generate_image
      why: image or audio content; media is out of scope for the text gate
  UNGOVERNED (no hooked stage): <unlisted tool>
  cannot govern:
    - PreToolUse rewrites arguments (`overwrite`, verified live on agy 1.5.5) only for run_command and read_file; every other tool, and an agy older than 1.5.4 (no hookEventName in the payload), is denied with the ctx command named
    - agy checks its permission rules against the rewritten command (`ctx run ...`), so where a rule pre-approves ctx but no rule covers the original command, the rewrite is sent as force_ask rather than approved
    - PostToolUse cannot replace output (its only legal output is {}): the result of a tool that was not rewritten reaches the transcript raw
    - grep_search, find_by_name and list_dir left agy's default toolset in 1.2.7; the model searches through run_command, which the command route governs
    - live agy 1.5.5 PostToolUse payloads carry no tool result at all, so the post stage records the call but captures nothing (decision no_result)
    - only tools named in the plugin's matchers are seen
